newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tajik group rejects firing of rebel colonel - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Tajik group rejects firing of rebel colonel - Tass.

text.p: A group set up by a rebel colonel to rule the southwest of Tajikistan refuses to recognise a presidential decree stripping him of command of an armed unit, Itar-Tass news agency said on Wednesday.

Kasim Babayev, a senior member of the "Defence Council", said it "disagreed with the president's decree on the dismissal of Colonel Makhmud Khudoyberdyev from his command of a motorised infantry brigade" and did not recognise his "retirement", the Russian agency reported.

Khudoyberdyev fought forces loyal to the government for four days after he moved his elite armoured brigade from the south towards Dushanbe when fighting broke out between two rival warlords in the capital on Saturday.
On Wednesday Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov's government said Khudoyberdyev had agreed to return to barracks and had been dismissed from his command.
But there has been no word from the renegade colonel on his dismissal while the defence council, located in the southern town of Kurgan Tyube, could not be reached for comment.

Khudoyberdyev, 34, imposed his control on Kurgan Tyube and surrounding areas in July. He has mutinied twice before to win concessions from Rakhmonov's weak administration but his current motives are unclear.

The government and Islamic opposition guerrillas, who are not linked to the latest unrest, signed an accord in June to end four years of civil war but gun law threatens the former Soviet republic's fragile peace.
